newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IPB main shareholder group holds 49 pct - SCP.
newsitem.headline: Czech IPB main shareholder group holds 49 pct - SCP.

text.p: The Czech securities centre (SCP) said on Tuesday that ownership of IPB a.s., the country's third largest bank by basic capital, was dominated by a group of 20 companies holding 49.4 percent of its shares.

State holdings in IPB, amounting to 36 percent, are due to be sold off in the middle of this year and local press reports say ING Bank and Japanese investment bank Nomura are front runners on the shortlist of buyers, which is being drawn up by U.S.-based investment bank Salomon Brothers.

The 20 companies, which vote together, are led by Charouz Holding a.s., with 11.9 percent, Bankovni Holding a.s., with 10.7 percent, Nutshell s.r.o., with 9.8 percent, and Vojenske Stavby a.s. with nine percent.

The Czech Republic's main privatisation fund, the National Property Fund (NPF), which currently holds 31.5 percent of the shares, will retain a golden share for a limited time after the sale is complete.
NPF chairman Roman Ceska, who does not have a seat in the cabinet which must approve the sale, has said Nomura has the best chance of winning the tender.
